I will keep my plan simple and steady. I have 90 mu, but my land is not all managed the same way because I run a wheat-maize system and I also plant stevia. Since some family members work off-farm, I will not make the farm too complicated. I will put 60 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 30 mu into stevia. I will stay with the crops I already know, use better seed where it helps me keep yield stable, and rely on my well irrigation at the key stages instead of watering too often. For wheat, I will push for a stable stand, enough fertilizer, and 3 irrigations because wheat in my area needs water at the important growth stages. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and keep field work lighter with no-tillage after wheat so I can save labor and catch the sowing window quickly. For stevia, I will manage it more carefully because it needs cleaner field management and more attention to fertilizer balance and pests, but I will still keep inputs moderate so the cost does not run too high. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield. I will aim for reliable output, manageable labor, and lower risk for my household.
